items.title: Noise rules: Sengkang names its 9 pickleball courts (from Nov. 1), and South Pasadena keeps courts open until 10 p.m.
items.summary: Singapore: from Nov. 1, Sengkang Town Council will allow pickleball at only nine approved courts, from 10 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. Pickleball will be banned at other courts that are too close to homes or where enough residents voted for a ban. The approved sites are Anchorvale Vista (near Blocks 310B and 312A), Aspella (275B), Compassvale North Gate (262C), Rivervale Gardens (120D), Rivervale Bank (121B), Rivervale View (161), Rivervale Shores (175) and Rivervale Haven (197). The council's Oct. 8 survey of 2,092 residents found 55.1% negatively affected, mostly by ball-impact noise. The Straits Times added the court list on Oct. 23. California: after almost two hours of public comment on Oct. 21, the South Pasadena City Council voted 3-1 to keep the Orange Grove and Garfield Park courts open until 10 p.m., rejecting a 9 p.m. recommendation. Opening time moves from 5 a.m. to 7 a.m. The council also approved, 4-0, one reservable court per park (up to 60 minutes) and permits for groups of 25+, leagues and other organized play. The rules are a six-month pilot that starts after the courts are resurfaced.

items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: judge signs interim DIP order (up to $4.365M); final hearing Nov. 10 in Dallas
items.summary: The DIP loan was the item we said was still pending yesterday. The bankruptcy court in the Northern District of Texas signed the interim DIP financing order on Oct. 21 (Dkt. 43 on the Omni Agent Solutions docket). It authorizes up to $4,365,000: $3.51 million in new-money term loans, of which up to $900,000 can be borrowed in the interim period, plus a roll-up of $850,000 in pre-petition bridge loans. The final DIP hearing is set for Nov. 10, 2026 at 2 p.m. CT, at 1100 Commerce St., Dallas. Objections are due Nov. 3. The order says that if no objections are filed, a final order may be entered without a hearing. Nothing in the order addresses club closures.

items.title: Screaming debate: Zane Navratil says players 'should be allowed to scream' and taunt
items.summary: Times Now reports that Zane Navratil said on Instagram that players should be allowed to scream and to taunt 'if they want.' Quotes: 'Let players act how they want and then let public opinion sort it out,' and 'We aren't role models, we're entertainers.' He argues that fans' reaction is a better penalty than losing a timeout. He points to the NFL's taunting rule ('the fans hated it') and to the UFC's trash talk as an example of how drama drives attention. Times Now notes that Navratil was criticized for yelling at an opponent during the MLP playoffs and later regretted it. This is a direct counterpoint to Jim Kloss's UPA anti-taunting proposal (warning, then loss of a timeout or challenge, then a mark), which we covered Oct. 16-21.

items.title: Noise rules spread in Singapore: Sengkang bans pickleball on some courts and limits hours from Nov. 1; Chua Chu Kang runs a foam-ball-only trial
items.summary: Mothership reports that Sengkang Town Council will ban pickleball from Nov. 1 on courts that are too close to residential blocks or that drew enough resident votes, citing MP Abdul Muhaimin's Oct. 21 Instagram post. Where pickleball is still allowed, play is limited to 10 a.m.-7:30 p.m. Banned courts will have their pickleball lines removed and signs posted. The council says residents voted these measures the most acceptable in a survey, and that it also considered distance to homes, sound frequency and site layout. Separately, Stomp reports that Chua Chu Kang Town Council is running a six-month 'use foam balls only' trial, started Oct. 1, at the court near Block 119A Plantation Crescent in Tengah. That court is open 9:30 a.m.-8 p.m. A council spokesperson confirmed on Oct. 22 that the trial is at that one court only, and said it will be evaluated before the council decides whether to continue. Mothership notes earlier steps: Holland-Bukit Panjang's 2025 ban, 9 a.m.-9 p.m. limits in some Ang Mo Kio estates, and Mountbatten's foam-ball sessions.

items.summary: After Monday's first-day hearing before Judge Scott W. Everett (U.S. Bankruptcy Court, N.D. items.title: UPA-A's Aspes pushes one paddle certification with USA Pickleball; Times Now amplifies the essay
items.summary: Times Now on Oct. 18 amplified UPA-A president Jason Aspes's Oct. 16 essay arguing that separate USA Pickleball and UPA-A paddle lists 'cost everyone.' Aspes proposes one approved list combining USA Pickleball's amateur/international reach with UPA-A's direct performance measurement, post-break-in testing, and independent labs, overseen by an independent technical committee with published methods/results/exceptions and no brand sponsorship ties. He criticizes aspects of OWL's USA Pickleball certification path and argues new-only testing can miss how paddles play after use. He also acknowledges UPA-A's own commercial ties to the pro leagues and says each side would have to give up control. Reddit's r/Pickleball had an 'USAP or UPA-A' thread Sunday. This is advocacy from UPA-A, not a deal between the two bodies.

items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: first-day court hearing set for Monday at 1:30 p.m. CT
items.summary: A notice filed Oct. 16 in The Picklr's Chapter 11 (Subchapter V) case sets an emergency first-day hearing for Monday, Oct. 19 at 1:30 p.m. CT. items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: local fallout and new filing details
items.summary: Business Journals in Houston, Orlando, Seattle and Philadelphia, plus AL.com, the Daily Press and MONTCO.Today, ran local angles in the past day.
